label: copy-phase input "h" fed back early in the copy (original positions 1-3)
explanation: Token-specific copy-phase feature: fires only when the fed-back input token is "h" during the copy phase, almost entirely when that h is original token 1, 2 or 3 (recall_idx 2-4) and is not the final output step. Strongest (activations near max) when h was original token 1 (prev2_tok = <DEL>, about 63% of mass), then original token 2. Weak/rare when h is echoed as original token 0 (recall_idx 1), and essentially silent when h is echoed at original position >= 4 or on the last step. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, never on any other input token (h in the original phase does not trigger it), and is insensitive to the output token, L, or digit count beyond these position effects.

issues: The core claims hold. All activation is in the copy phase, and 39008 of 39012 active steps have in_tok h. Mass by recall_idx: 2 has 63.4%, 3 has 32.6%, 4 has 2.3%, 1 has 1.7%. On to_go==0 (the last step) the feature fires with precision 0.017. Output token and n_digits make no difference.

The predicate's recall_idx 4 is a systematic false-positive class, so the 'original positions 1-3' label overclaims. For copy-phase h with recall_idx 4 and to_go>=1, precision is only 0.39 (11108 predicted). By L it is 0.37 at L=6, 0.46 at L=7, 0.43 at L=8 and 0.31 at L=9. This class makes up most of the 6689 test false positives, for example 'a d f h 0 3 x x <DEL> a d f *h*'. By contrast, recall_idx 2-3 with to_go>=1 has precision 0.9995. Splitting recall_idx 4 by in_count, digits or prev_tok did not separate the cases where it fires.

The explanation says the feature 'does not depend on L' and fires 'weakly and rarely' on recall_idx 1. That is false for short sequences. Precision for copy-phase h at recall_idx 1 is 0.51 at L=3, 0.65 at L=4 and 0.48 at L=5, then falls to 0.22 at L=6, 0.08 at L=7, 0.03 at L=8 and 0.05 at L=9. So whether it fires when h is original token 0 depends strongly on L (equivalently on absolute t). These are the misses in test, e.g. 'h z g m 0 <DEL> [h:0.05]'.

Test F1 for the original predicate is 0.860. Dropping recall_idx 4 gives 0.871 (precision 0.999, recall 0.771). Adding recall_idx 1 for L<=5 gives 0.887. Further adding recall_idx 4 for L in {7,8} gives 0.888. The gaps are small in activation mass but systematic.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input "h" when it was original token 1 or 2 (recall_idx 2-3), not on the last step; also fires partially when h was original token 0 in short sequences (L<=5) and when h was original token 3 (about 40% of the time)
